title: Data centers are turning to old jet engines as the wait for power grows
slides: Why would data centers bolt on old jet engines?
Grid connections now take years, not months
Aircraft turbines produce power in weeks instead
Your cloud costs may shift as operators improvise
Ask providers how they secure power for 2027
thread_text:
1. Jet engines for data centers?

AI's power demand is so high that operators are repurposing aircraft turbines to keep servers running, bypassing years-long grid delays.

2. Grid connections now take years

What used to be a months-long process now stretches to 2027 or beyond, forcing companies to find creative workarounds.

3. Turbines deliver power in weeks

Unlike slow grid upgrades, aircraft turbines can be installed and operational in a fraction of the time, bridging the gap.

4. Your cloud bill may rise

As operators improvise with costly stopgap solutions, those expenses could trickle down to your monthly cloud costs.

5. Ask about 2027 power plans

When negotiating cloud contracts, demand specifics: how will your provider secure power for 2027? Get it in writing.

instagram.caption:
Grid connections for new data centers now stretch to 2027 or beyond — so operators are bolting old aircraft turbines onto buildings to keep servers running.

A grid hookup used to take months. Now it takes years, and AI's power demand won't wait. ✈️

Aircraft turbines can be installed and producing power in weeks instead.

Those stopgap fixes cost money, and operators may pass the expense down to your monthly cloud bill. 💸

If you build or publish with cloud tools, ask your provider one question before signing: how exactly will you secure power for 2027? Get the answer in writing. ⚡

Would you pay more for cloud services if it meant guaranteed uptime? 🤔
